title: Cypress POC: Warmstart vs Coldstart Latency & Cost Scan
summary: Workshop-driven benchmark capturing warmstart vs coldstart behavior for multi-model setups and cost projections for a mid-size retail chatbot POC. Focus: p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput (tokens/sec), coldstart penalty, warm cache hit dynamics, and cost per 1M tokens under hosted vs reserved capacity with burst. Key outcome: warm cache and model co-location yield large p95 improvements (>3x) for tail latency, but introduce cost tradeoffs that favor reserved capacity for steady QPS; fallback/heterogeneous routing reduces P99 under burst.
objectives:
- Measure coldstart penalty (model load + kv-cache priming) across 3 model variants
- Characterize warm cache hit curve over 30-minute traffic windows
- Evaluate multi-model fallback (large -> quantized) effect on latency and cost under burst
- Produce cost model for hosted (on-demand) vs reserved capacity with 20% burst allowance
test_configuration:
Models: redwood-7b-qat (8-bit), rwd-7b-pt (fp16), open-13b-fp16 as fallback.
Hardware: A100-80GB (hosted pool), T4 equivalent (edge sim).
Runtime: Redwood serving runtime 2.4.1 with continuous batching on, KV cache enabled, cache-ttl 15m.
Workload: 75% short queries (~16 tokens output), 25% long (~120 tokens). Sequence length token gen capped at 256.
Concurrency targets: steady 60 qps, burst to 240 qps for 90s.
Batch windows: auto-batching (up to 128 tokens), max-latency-slo 250ms for p95 target.
Routing policy: prefer rwd-7b-pt for quality, fallback to redwood-7b-qat for cost when latency degradation or capacity limits reached.
methodology: Load generation using locust-based driver instrumented with token-level tracing. Each scenario run for 20 minutes steady-state, followed by 10 minute burst. Coldstart measurement performed by draining the model instance pool and issuing first-request spikes; measured from client request to first token emitted. Warmstart measured after 10-minute steady traffic window. All experiments repeated 3x; reported numbers are the median across repetitions. Metric capture: p50/p95/p99 latencies (ms), tokens/sec, model load time (ms), cache hit ratio, host GPU utilization, and estimated cost per 1M tokens (USD) using internal pricing assumptions. Logs linked in artifacts.
results:
Scenario A — Warm: steady 60 qps on rwd-7b-pt (A100): p50=42ms, p95=118ms, p99=210ms, throughput=18k tokens/sec, cache-hit=82%.
Scenario B — Cold (first wave after idle): coldstart model load=2.1s median, p95 first-requests=1.9s, repeated cold cycles reduce p95 to ~320ms after 1 minute as cache primes.
Scenario C — Burst to 240 qps with routing (prefer pt, fallback to qat): p50=68ms, p95=310ms, p99=650ms; fallback reduced p99 by ~32% compared to strict single-model queuing, but average cost increased by 12%.
Scenario D — T4 edge sim (warm) running qat: p50=95ms, p95=420ms, p99=980ms, throughput=6.5k tokens/sec.
Notes: cache warmup contributes ~60–75% of the p95 improvement between cold and warm. Model load accounts for the remaining tail. Quantized model (qat) has 1.6x lower tokens/sec cost but adds 10–25% extra latency on long generations compared to fp16 variant.
cost_modeling:
Assumptions: Hosted on-demand unit cost: $0.28/hr per A100 equivalent; Reserved monthly (committed) amortized: $0.12/hr per A100 equivalent. Token compute cost estimate derived from tokens/sec and instance-hours used.
Hosted summary (mixed traffic, including bursts): estimated $18.4 per 1M tokens.
Reserved summary (steady 60 qps with 20% burst margin): estimated $7.9 per 1M tokens.
Fallback strategy cost delta: adding quantized fallback increases hosted cost by ~12% (more instances used during burst) but cuts tail outages.
Recommendation: For sustained >40 qps workloads, reserved capacity yields ~2.3x cost savings; for spiky / low baseline workloads, hosted on-demand still reasonable but combine with model warm pools for critical endpoints to reduce coldstart exposure.
analysis_and_findings:
1) Warm cache is the dominant factor for tail latency improvement — prioritized cache sharing heuristics (prefix affinity, session affinity) reduce p95 significantly.
2) Coldstart is driven by two components: container/model load (~1.5–2.5s) and KV-cache warm priming (~0.2–0.4s per request while priming). First-request SLOs must account for model load unless a warm pool is maintained.
3) Multi-model fallback reduces p99 during bursts but increases overall token cost unless routing prioritizes cost thresholds and only activates fallback under defined capacity pressure.
4) Quantization (8-bit) is an effective cost tool but can degrade long-generation latency and occasionally output quality; recommend A/Bing on evaluation prompts before production rollout.
5) Edge-class hardware significantly increases tail; plan conservative SLAs or local fallback to smaller models.
recommendations:
- Implement a small warm-pool (reserved) for high-priority chat endpoints to eliminate model coldstart (cost ~2–4% of reserved footprint but reduces first-request p95 by >90%).
- Enable cross-variant cache sharing when session semantics allow (same tokenizer/architecture families) to accelerate priming.
- Use routing rules: prefer fp16 model until latency/degradation thresholds or queue depth triggers fallback to quantized model. Tune fallback hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping.
- For customers with steady medium QPS (>40), propose reserved capacity contract; include 20% burst buffer and automated overflow to hosted spot instances.
- Add cost-aware telemetry to routes (token-level cost estimate per request) to enable dynamic decisions.
- Run a 2-week field trial with reserved warm-pool enabled and monitor p99, cost curve, and quality regressions.
